$comment: permissions.create -> POST /drive/v3/files/{fileId}/permissions, request+response Permission. Read from the Drive v3 discovery document 2026-09-30. Scope unchanged: drive.file already covers sharing a file this app created. `emailAddress` is marked output-only in the discovery schema's general description, which is a known quirk of Google's generated docs for this endpoint -- it is the documented, required field for granting a user or group permission on create; Google's own Permissions guide confirms it.
title: Share a Google Drive file
description: Grant a user, group, domain, or anyone with the link access to a file.
$idempotencyComment: permissions.create has no documented idempotency key. Calling it twice for the same grantee and role creates a SECOND permission resource rather than refusing or returning the first -- Drive does not deduplicate by grantee.

query.$comment: Fixed to false rather than exposed as a choice: this connector has no email content vocabulary for the invitation Drive would otherwise send, and a silently-sent email to a grantee with no context is worse than none. A host wanting notification can send its own.

config.label: Role
config.description: organizer, fileOrganizer and owner exist in Drive's API but only apply inside a shared drive, which this action does not target.

config.label: Email address
config.description: Required when the grantee type is a person or a Google Group. Ignored for domain and anyone.

config.label: Domain
config.description: Required when the grantee type is domain, e.g. example.com. Ignored otherwise.

outputShape.description: Present for a user or group grant.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
